To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(0),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(0)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(0))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(0).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(0)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(0) & =x \\ f(x) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,3.\end{aligned}
$$

We discard $x=0$ since the logarithm is not defined here. Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(0)=3.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2) \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)+\frac{{x}^{2}}{x-2} \\ {f}^{′}(3) & =2\cdot 3\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-2)+\frac{{3}^{2}}{3-2} \\ {f}^{′}(3) & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(0) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(0))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
